The Taylor coefficient \(d_n\) equals the coefficient of \(x^n\) in the expansion of \(f\) about \(0\).  
Since the only singularity on the circle of convergence \(|x|=1\) is the simple pole at \(x=1\), the limit of the coefficients is the residue of \(f\) at that pole:

\[
\operatorname{Res}_{x=1} f(x)=\frac{(2025+1)\ln(2025+1)}{(1-2)(1-3)}=\frac{2026\ln 2026}{2}=1013\ln 2026.
\]

All other singularities lie outside the unit circle and their contributions vanish as \(n\to\infty\). Hence  

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} d_n = 1013\ln 2026.
\]

**ANSWER: 1013 ln 2026**
